comment: Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: option-click moves the text cursor
Tooltip for the “⌥-Click moves cursor” checkbox in Settings > Pointer
english: If enabled, option-click sends arrow keys to move the cursor's position. If Shell Integration is installed then it does not take effect at the command line.

comment: Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: a three-finger tap acts as a middle click
Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: command-click opens the filename or URL under the pointer
Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: keyboard focus follows the mouse pointer
Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: right or middle click also focuses the window
english: Focus window after right or middle click

comment: Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: horizontal scroll events are reported to apps that use mouse reporting
Tooltip for the horizontal scrolling mouse reporting checkbox in Settings > Pointer
english: When enabled, mouse reporting takes priority over swipe to switch tabs. Disable this if swiping to switch tabs sometimes doesn’t work.

comment: Section label in Settings > Pointer > General, to the left of the click settings
Section label in Settings > Pointer > General, to the left of the focus settings
Section label in Settings > Pointer > General, to the left of the mouse reporting settings
Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: control-click is sent to apps instead of opening the context menu
english: ^-Click reported to apps, does not open menu

comment: Tooltip for the control-click mouse reporting checkbox in Settings > Pointer
english: For terminal applications that use mouse reporting, turning this on allows control-click to be reported instead of opening the context menu.

comment: Checkbox in Settings > Pointer > General: right click is sent to apps instead of opening the context menu
english: Right click reported to apps, does not open menu

comment: Tooltip for the right-click mouse reporting checkbox in Settings > Pointer
english: For terminal applications that use mouse reporting, turning this on allows right click (or two finger tap on a trackpad) to be reported instead of opening the context menu.
